lessons.claim: A single chain **cannot yield a bulk G' or G'' [Pa]** -- what is legitimate has to be distinguished from what is not. ✅ Legitimate: K*[kT/d²] → EI[N·m²] → κ₀[N/m] (a purely geometric conversion). Measured, JKR gives κ₀=56.6 mN/m, but that is **a round-trip confirmation recovering the input 64 mN/m** and not a verification (the -12% is the finite trap + viscous contamination at De=10.7). What is meaningful is that DLVO gives -0.005 mN/m, 4~5 orders below. ❌ Illegitimate: applying GSER `G* = K*/(6πa)` gives JKR G'=15.6 Pa and G''=7.9 Pa, but it is **invalid** -- GSER holds when the probe is immersed in a continuous medium, whereas here what the bead feels is not a medium but 2 neighbouring beads. To produce a real G'(ω) you have to build a **network** of chains and compute it directly from the stress tensor. Multiplying a single chain by an assumed areal density is inventing. ※ chain-bend-2d-oscill's observation.yaml F1 had already written the same warning, and it is now quantitatively confirmed.
